analysis: Examined the head-side test-only unit of GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift (lines 509-941). The change adds tests for GLM5 prompt policy: thinking-object controls, OpenRouter reasoning/reasoning_details replay, captured strict tool requests, empty history arguments, clear_thinking precedence, large-number schema handling, and forged internal marker rejection (lines 603-619). No production code is changed in this unit, so no control, trust boundary, key, attestation, cache or authorization behavior is altered. Tests cover security-relevant input validation: coordinator-owned marker `x-darkbloom-original-boolean-schema` is rejected only when the actual model type is glm5_next (lines 603-619), integer enum overflow is rejected before rounding (lines 899-908), duplicate-key and non-object tool arguments are rejected (lines 567-575), and malformed aliases are refused (lines 630-635). Line 615-616 intentionally documents that non-GLM model types retain old tolerance of the markers; this is pre-existing behavior, not a regression. T-041 was supplied but is unrelated to this prompt-policy test file. The patch excerpt is truncated and the production changes implementing the new thinking, reasoning_details and strict-tool handling were not supplied. Whether those changes affect prompt-injection, reasoning-content leakage or tool-schema handling cannot be judged from this unit, so integration should examine GLM5NextPromptPolicy and ProviderPromptContractPipeline sources. A test comment at line 713-719 shows stale or conflicting reasoning fields are dropped in favor of reasoning_content, which looks consistent with deterministic precedence.
